title: Intrinsic-Motivated Sensor Management: Exploring with Physical Surprise

problem.claim: Sensor management must improve monitoring capabilities from real-time data in complex physical systems with expanded sensor coverage.

gap.claim: Existing model-based and learning-based sensor-management methods are limited by system-specific knowledge requirements, overfitting, inaccurate physics modeling, and convergence failure in complex uncertain scenarios.

contributions.claim: This work introduces a sensor-management approach that combines physics embedding and self-supervised reinforcement learning, driven by an intrinsic reward.
Intrinsic-motivated sensor management constructs local surprise information from physical latent features to capture hidden states and motivate faster exploration.
The proposed model is implemented for unmanned-vehicle sensor management and sensor rescheduling in complex or settled power systems, with or without observability constraints.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the designs relieve inconsistency with underlying physics or physical dynamics and adapt the global monitoring-capability objective to local environmental changes.
The authors report experimental effectiveness on physical-system sensor control.
Numerical results are reported to show consistently higher threat-detection accuracy and better observability recovery than existing methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Complex physical systems have broader sensor coverage but face greater difficulty using real-time data for monitoring.
Existing model-based and learning-based approaches face system-specific limitations, overfitting, inaccurate physics modeling, and convergence failure.
The paper introduces physics-embedded, self-supervised reinforcement learning with intrinsic surprise derived from physical latent features.
The method is reported to improve physics consistency, adapt to local changes, and support sensor-control applications.
Numerical results are reported to improve threat-detection accuracy and observability recovery over existing methods.

source_observation.claim: Physical latent features and local surprise information are used as an intrinsic reward for exploration in sensor management.

interpretation.claim: Exploration signals derived from domain-relevant hidden-state information may help learning-based control respond to complex physical environments.

application.claim: Use domain-informed intrinsic rewards when reinforcement learning must manage sensing under uncertain physical dynamics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported physical-system sensor-control settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the physical latent-feature construction or intrinsic-reward formula.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, numerical effect sizes, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
